To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a fast and robust signal processing method for the thermoelastic stress analysis of cyclic loaded samples using a single point infrared scanner.

the use of a fast infrared scanning system and an extended data sampling window allows the acquisition and processing of the thermoelastic signal at low cost and with a high temporal resolution, which is of great interest in the area of dynamic stress analysis.

a fast infrared scanner is capable of acquiring thermoelastic data with a high spatial and temporal resolution, which allows for a detailed investigation of the temperature field evolution during cyclic loading.

the development of an optical method to detect the thermoelastic effect in materials and to determine the stress distribution on the surface of a specimen.
the development of a fast infrared scanner for thermoelastic stress analysis (TSA) and the development of a lock-in based signal processing algorithm for the acquisition of the thermoelastic signal.
the use of the Thermoelastic effect for stress measurements in materials.
